answer: Admission is a published itinerary, not an open signup. A new identity locks fees behind unique, re-executable job artifacts. Midway through that voyage, an established auditor from a distant co-signature cluster, like a falcon stooping on one unannounced waypoint, re-runs the artifact and posts the digest. Voting weight vests only after every waypoint is independently reproduced and no other key has claimed those hashes, then thaws on a glacier calendar, one slice per epoch. Duplicate itineraries collide and locked fees are slashed, so clones must buy fresh unique work, not extra keys.
